expectations.text: validate_skill.py reports 0 errors on the written skill folder
The skill states the 500-character limit per section and gives the reason (the Play Store cuts off longer text)
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md line 8: 'The Play Store cuts off anything past 500 characters mid-sentence, and we hold the iOS section to the same limit so the two stay the same length.' The script enforces LIMIT = 500.

expectations.text: The skill says PRs labelled internal or chore are never mentioned and that no ticket or PR numbers appear
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md line 10: 'PRs labelled `internal` or `chore` are never mentioned, not even reworded.' Step 4: 'No PR or ticket numbers. Strip them from titles before you rewrite.' The script flags #\d+, ABC-123 and 'PR 123' patterns.

expectations.text: The skill gives the hotfix branch with the exact line "Bug fixes and performance improvements."
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md step 2: 'both sections are exactly this one line and nothing else:' followed by 'Bug fixes and performance improvements.' Caveat not covered by the assertion: the same step says 'Skip to step 5', which skips step 4, where release-notes.md is written.

expectations.text: The skill's description has a "Not for" clause covering PR descriptions or the internal changelog
expectations.evidence: Description ends: 'Not for PR descriptions or the internal CHANGELOG.md.'

expectations.text: The skill's definition of done includes checking each section's character count
expectations.evidence: 'Done when' line 54: 'The check prints PASS, and both character counts are shown to the user.' The script prints '<name>: <count>/500 characters'.

expectations.text: An evals.md next to the written SKILL.md holds 5-8 test prompts, including one that should not trigger the skill and one that leaves out a key input
expectations.evidence: No evals.md anywhere in old_skill/outputs (files: app-whats-new/, app-whats-new.zip, handoff.md, run-notes.md, script-tests/*.md). handoff.md 'Road-test plan' gives only 3 prompts inline (normal release, hotfix, should-not-trigger), with no missing-key-input prompt. That is below the 5-8 required for a team skill.

claims.claim: check_notes.py flags overflow, #4312, JIRA-881, crash and markdown
claims.evidence: script-tests/bad.md exists, and the code has these patterns. Spot test: a file with '- ' bullets FAILs as 'markdown formatting', matching its plain-text-only rule.

claims.claim: Judgment check 'Every instruction exact or explained: pass'
claims.evidence: The hotfix step says 'Skip to step 5', which skips step 4 (writing release-notes.md), yet step 5 checks that file. A literal agent could run the check on a file that does not exist. No cold read was done to catch this (run-notes: 'Subagents: None started').

claims.claim: The prior failure 'Refactor auth module (#4312)' was labelled internal
claims.evidence: SKILL.md line 44 states it was 'labelled `internal`', but the user only said it was 'internal work'. This invented detail hides the case where such a PR is unlabelled, which the skill has no path for.

claims.claim: Zip has the folder at its root

uncertainties: Confirmation gate skipped since user unavailable
'Same length' read as identical lines except platform-only
Hotfix detection: user says so or every PR has hotfix label, else ask
How a release's PRs are defined
${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} used with a fallback for claude.ai
workarounds: First script-test loop passed '--hotfix' as part of the filename (zsh word splitting); fixed in the test harness

suggestions.assertion: validate_skill.py reports 0 errors on the written skill folder
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfied: a careless skill with only name+description and no real content would also pass validate_skill.py with 0 errors. It is a floor check, not a discriminator.

suggestions.assertion: The written skill's SKILL.md frontmatter uses only the portable fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools), because the skill must also run on claude.ai
suggestions.reason: Also passes for a careless output; nearly every generated skill uses only name+description. It only discriminates if the run is tempted to add Claude Code-only fields (argument-hint, etc.).

suggestions.assertion: The skill's definition of done includes checking each section's character count
suggestions.reason: Passes for any skill that says 'show the character counts'. It does not check that counting is actually enforced by a script or how newlines/bullets/emoji are counted, which is where the real 900-char failure would recur.

suggestions.assertion: An evals.md next to the written SKILL.md holds 5-8 test prompts, including one that should not trigger the skill and one that leaves out a key input
suggestions.reason: 'Next to the written SKILL.md' conflicts with skill-builder/SKILL.md line 110 ('saved as evals.md next to the skill'). with_skill put it beside the skill folder (outputs/evals.md) on purpose so it does not ship in the zip. Reword the assertion to 'next to the skill folder (not inside it)' or decide which is wanted.

No assertion checks the 'hidden knowledge' answers: features before fixes and 'stability improvements' instead of 'crash'. Both runs include them, but a run that dropped them would still pass all 8 assertions.

No assertion checks how the skill handles the user's own failure example: 'Refactor auth module' is internal work, but the user never said it carried the internal label. Under the user's definition an unlabelled refactor is user-facing. with_skill handles this (generic stability line + flag as possibly mislabelled, ask for labels if none); old_skill assumes it was labelled internal and has no path for an unlabelled list. This is the most discriminating gap between the runs.

No assertion checks that the hotfix branch still produces release-notes.md. old_skill's step 2 says 'Skip to step 5', which skips step 4 (writing the file) before running the check; with_skill's cold read caught and fixed this exact bug. An assertion like 'the hotfix branch writes release-notes.md and then runs the check' would discriminate.

No assertion checks the 'every user-facing PR covered' done-criterion is made visible (e.g. a coverage table or counts that add up). Both runs have it, but it is the guard against the lazy 'drop PRs to fit 500' failure.

eval_feedback.overall: Only assertion #8 failed, and only because this skill-builder version produced a 3-prompt inline plan, not an evals.md. The assertions miss this run's more serious flaws: the hotfix 'skip to step 5' bug and no handling of unlabelled PRs.
